title: MailboxFilterCondition.parent_id public API break not flagged
description:
Commit 869f7fb changed MailboxFilterCondition.parent_id from Option<Id> to Option<serde_json::Value> at crate-jmap-mail-types/src/mailbox.rs:238. The struct is #[non_exhaustive] (construction-side break is mitigated) but read-side access (cond.parent_id matching, destructuring) goes from one type to another — any consumer that did 'if let Some(id) = cond.parent_id { ... }' assuming Id will fail to compile, and consumers that pattern-matched will silently change behaviour.

Two problems:

1. The commit subject is 'refactor(mail-server): push Mailbox/query filter+sort into backend' — no exclamation mark, no warning about a type-crate public-API break. SemVer convention (and the workspace cookie-cutter rule) is to use 'refactor!' or 'feat!' when public types break.

2. jmap-mail-types is currently at version 0.1.1 on crates.io. The next published version will silently carry a public type change. Pre-1.0 SemVer permits this but downstream consumers using ^0.1 ranges will pull the breaking change without warning. The version should bump to 0.2 (pre-1.0 breaking-change convention) and CHANGELOG/release-notes should call out the break.

The type-change itself is justified: serde's default Option<T> Deserialize collapses JSON null to None, which would defeat the three-way absent/null/string parentId distinction required by RFC 8621 §2.3. The fix is correct. The packaging story is the gap.
close_reason: CHANGELOG.md (65ea6584) records the MailboxFilterCondition.parent_id type change under 0.2.0.
